title: Fewer barrels, dirtier barrels: The hidden environmental cost of US sanctions on Venezuela’s oil
summary: After US sanctions, Venezuela flared more than twice as much gas for each barrel of oil it produced, as shortages of imported diluent overloaded its oil infrastructure.

title: How pension cuts push households to save more and work longer
summary: In urban China, cuts to pension generosity in 1997 and 2005 led households to save more and work longer, explaining around a quarter of the rise in the household saving rate and half the rise in working hours between 1995 and 2009.

title: Do women underreport domestic violence to male enumerators?
summary: Women in Bangladesh reported more intimate partner violence to female survey enumerators than their male counterparts, changing impact estimates of BRAC’s Ultra-Poor Graduation programme.

title: How does progressive taxation shape revenue and incidence in low-capacity states?

title: When does irrigation reduce migration pressure? Evidence from West Africa
summary: Drought makes rural households in West Africa more likely to consider moving, and irrigation only helps them stay when droughts are prolonged, mainly for the richest households.

title: Making tax collection cheaper could unlock growth
summary: Low-income countries collect as little as $30 in tax for every dollar they spend collecting it. High-income countries collect $270. New research suggests that improving the efficiency of how taxes are collected could significantly lift the GDP of low-income countries.

title: Can correcting misconceptions about therapy help students seek care?
summary: Evidence from a survey experiment in Mexico shows that correcting misconceptions about therapy makes university students more likely to share counselling information with peers, while raising therapy use only among students who had recently used it.

title: Implementation science in education: Scaling what works

title: When cheaper job ads lead to harder-to-fill jobs
summary: In Ethiopia, subsidising vacancy-posting costs leads small and medium-sized enterprises to advertise publicly and create more white-collar positions, which they then struggle to fill.
